# `conditionalFormatConfigs`: the conditional-format rule records

Part of [generated data](../generated-data.md). How rules are read, and why a record's key is content: [conditional format rules](../architecture/conditional-format-rules.md).

## How `conditionalFormatConfigs` is generated

**`conditionalFormatConfigs`** (`generated/conditionalFormatConfigs.ts`) is generated by `ConditionalFormatConfigOperator` (`05_Operators`) from the rules the regen's sheet-properties get brought into Raw, after the config sync, so it costs no round trip of its own. `RuleRecords.build` (`configReaders/RuleRecords.ts`) turns each tab's rules into records, one per rule, in sheet order. `makeConditionalFormatConfigs` validates nothing beyond the type.

## The file's shape: `tables` and `tabs`

The literal has two groups:

- **`tables`**, by Table key, holds the rules whose range touches a Table with API access. A record names its `tableId`.
- **`tabs`**, by tab name, holds every other rule on that tab. A record names its `sheetGid`.

Within a group each record is keyed by its rule handle, and each record is one of two kinds:

- **A boolean record** (`kind: "boolean"`) holds its `condition` and its `format` (`backgroundColor` and `foregroundColor` as hex). A Table record names its `columns`, a list of column names or `"all"`, and writes a custom formula in brace form; a tab record names its A1 `ranges`.
- **An unmodelable record** (`kind: "unmodelable"`) holds its A1 `ranges` and its `rawContent`, the JSON of the rule without its ranges. A Table's boolean rule becomes one when a range doesn't start on the Table's first body row or leaves its body, or when its formula has no brace form.

## The rule handle

A boolean record's handle is `<scope> | <condition> | <format>`: the scope is its columns joined by `+` (or `all`) on a Table, its A1 ranges joined by `,` on a tab; the condition is the formula, or the condition type and its JSON values; the format is `background <hex>` and `text <hex>`, joined by `, `. An unmodelable record's handle is `<ranges> | unmodelable <rawContent>`. A repeat of a handle in the same group takes `-2`, `-3` and so on, in sheet order.
